answer: Per-key sequential delay requires each new agent identity to solve a unique memory-hard chain seeded by its public key before any task is accepted. A lantern-lit audit log stores checkpoints, so cloned keys fail replay. An honest agent signs one history with a quill and reuses it. Cloning costs 15 minutes CPU and 2 GB RAM per identity plus a fresh onyx-marked checkpoint, making mass duplication pricier than one truthful record.
